courseTitle: 100 Days of Code: JavaScript Data Structures and Algorithms

lectures.title: What is an Array? Why do we need it?

cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to talk about what is an array in JavaScript.
So array is the most used data structure.
An array is a simple collection of objects or things.
They are very powerful data structures that store list of elements and they have endless applications.
Simple examples can be collection of books on your table, clothes in your wardrobe, or pens in your
pen stand.
So let's quickly examine an example from the real life.
Imagine you have a various items that you want to organize and manage, such as your favorite objects,
books, or balls.
We can put them in a large container with labeled sections for different items, so we can put the books
in books compartment, and we can put the bolts in both compartments, and we can put the gifts in the
gifts compartment, which are our favorite objects.
So this container helps you to keep the track of your collection and makes it easy to access and manage
the items.
Now you can think of an array as a large container with separate sections to store each item.
So we can express this in terms of array like this.
So here also we have the different compartments in a big container contiguously.
So they have to locate next to each other.
So as you can see in case of our container we can access each compartment using their labels.
We know that in books we have books in balls we have balls and in GIFs we have GIF.
But in case of array, we can access these compartments with their indexes, which starts from zero.
So for the first one we can access it with index of zero, and for the second one with index of one.
And it continues like this.
The array in JavaScript is different than the arrays, for example in Java, because in Java the arrays
are homogeneous, which means that they have to store same type of data, but in case of JavaScript
they are not homogeneous.
You can insert any type of data in the array.
So as you can see here we have string type and integer type.
So we are going to learn about different types of arrays in JavaScript in our upcoming lectures.
So I don't want to go to the details over here.
But here you just need to know that the arrays are not homogeneous in JavaScript.
Now you might be interested.
Why do we need an array?
So in software program array is used almost everywhere in the program to store the data.
Consider a situation where we need to store three integer numbers.
If we use the programming simple variable and data type concepts, we need three variables of integer
data type and we can declare them separately.
So as you can see, it is very simple because we had to store just three integer numbers.
Now let's assume we have to store 500 integer numbers.
Are we going to use 500 variables?
Of course not, because our code will be long and we will not be able to support it in the future.
So to handle such situations.
Almost all programming languages provide a concept called array.
An array is a data structure which can store a collection of elements.
So instead of declaring individual variables such as number one, number two until number 500, you
can just declare an array and represent individual variables inside this array.
Then we can access the elements by using their indexes in JavaScript.
Memory allocation for arrays is managed by JavaScript engine.
So you don't need to allocate memory like you would do in other programming languages.
When you create an array in JavaScript, memory is automatically allocated to store the elements.
So Java Engine handles memory allocation and deallocation using garbage collector, which reclaims memory
for objects and arrays that are no longer in use.
